# Balanced one-pulse Kerr: deterministic endpoint amplitudes

13 November 2026. **Proved at the endpoint-amplitude scope below.** Read current
STATE/TRAPS and the checked real-Hiary/Gaussian reduction. No code, numerical
tests, network, API, Git, archives, or shared-status edits. The argument uses
certified polynomial interpolation of the binomial weight; no growing-degree
Hermite or Krawtchouk asymptotic theorem is assumed.

## Statement and exact conventions

Let K>=0 be binary, zeta=a/b rational in binary, p>=1, and 0<=r<=K with
min(r,K-r)<=Y. There is a deterministic algorithm, polynomial in

    Y, bitlength(K+1), bitlength(a/b), p,

which approximates to absolute error 2^-p the complex number

    A_r = 1/sqrt(C(K,r)) sum_{n=0}^K P_K(n) K_r(K-n) e(zeta binom(n,2)),
    P_K(n)=2^-K C(K,n),  e(t)=exp(2 pi i t),
    K_r(x)=[z^r](1-z)^x(1+z)^(K-x).

This is the sum specified in the task. For the literal convention
B(theta)=exp(theta(a†b-b†a)), both rotations +pi/4, and n/r counting mode a,
the physical amplitude is **(-1)^(K+r) A_r**. Indeed
B a† B^-1=(a†-b†)/sqrt2, B b† B^-1=(a†+b†)/sqrt2. The first rotation
contributes (-1)^(K-n), while the second matrix entry contains
(-1)^n K_r(n); use K_r(n)=(-1)^r K_r(K-n). This known output sign costs
nothing, but should not be silently dropped from a complex-amplitude contract.

Two exact polynomial identities pay the endpoint reduction:

    K_r(K-n)=sum_{j=0}^r (-1)^(r-j) 2^j C(K-j,r-j) C(n,j),             (1)
    K_{K-s}(x)=(-1)^x K_s(x),  integer 0<=x<=K.                         (2)

For (1), expand (1-z)^K(1+2z/(1-z))^n. For (2), take the reciprocal
degree-K generating polynomial. Thus (1) has degree r and leading coefficient
2^r/r!. For an upper endpoint r=K-s, replace r by s, multiply by (-1)^K,
and add 1/2 to the linear phase in n. Normalization C(K,K-s)=C(K,s) is
unchanged. It suffices henceforth to compile the lower endpoint and an
arbitrary rational linear/quadratic phase e(A n+B n^2); originally
A=-zeta/2, B=zeta/2. The upper-endpoint shift is exact.

At integer 0<=n<=K, the generating formula and Vandermonde's identity give
|K_r(K-n)|<=C(K,r)<=(K+1)^r. Also 1/sqrt(C(K,r))<=1.
The integer C(K,r) has O(r log(K+1)) bits and is computed with r factors.

## 1. A central window and the only direct branch

K=0 is immediate. Put ell=bitlength(K+1) and

    Q=p+(r+1)ell+20,  J=2048 Q.

If K<=2^30 Q^2, evaluate the original finite sum directly. The number of
terms and even expanded factorial/binomial bit lengths are then polynomial
in the declared resources. The criterion is an exact integer comparison;
it does not presume K is small because its binary encoding is short.

In the other branch put c=K/2, w=ceil(sqrt(KQ)),
L=ceil(c-w), U=floor(c+w), M=U-L. Integer square root gives the endpoints
exactly. The chosen cutoff implies w<K/4 and w>J/2+1, so 0<=L<U<=K.
For a Bin(K,1/2) variable, Hoeffding's bound gives

    sum_{n outside [L,U]} P_K(n) <=2 exp(-2w^2/K)<=2 exp(-2Q).

Consequently deleting this tail changes A_r by at most
2^(r ell+1-2Q)<2^(-p-20), uniformly in the phase. This pays the potentially
large polynomial factor before making any approximation to the central weight.

## 2. Entire-function bound for the binomial weight

For proof only, extend P_K to the entire function

    f(c+u)=2^-K Gamma(K+1)/[Gamma(c+u+1)Gamma(c-u+1)].

Euler's product for Gamma, with the two opposite shifts paired, gives the
locally uniformly convergent product

    f(c+u)=f(c) product_{l=0}^infinity (1-u^2/(c+1+l)^2).              (3)

This identity also follows directly by taking the paired finite products
in Euler's limit formula; their exponential powers cancel. Duplication and
the beta integral give

    f(c)=Gamma(c+1/2)/(sqrt(pi)Gamma(c+1))
        =(1/pi) integral_0^1 t^(c-1/2)(1-t)^(-1/2) dt <=1.

Since sum_{l>=0}(c+1+l)^(-2)<=1/c=2/K, (3) proves for EVERY complex u

    |f(c+u)| <= exp(2|u|^2/K).                                      (4)

No complex Gamma evaluation is needed by the algorithm.

Choose J+1 consecutive integer nodes n_i=n_0+i, with
n_0=floor(c)-J/2, 0<=i<=J. They lie in [L,U]. Let I_J be their exact
degree-J interpolation polynomial for f. On the circle |z-c|=8w,
(4) gives |f(z)|<=exp(128w^2/K)<=exp(512Q)<=2^(1024Q).
For every real n in [L,U], the contour interpolation remainder is bounded by

    |f(n)-I_J(n)|
      <= (8/7) 2^(1024Q) (2/7)^(J+1)
      <= 2^(1024Q-J) = 2^(-1024Q).                                  (5)

Here |n-n_i|<=2w, |z-n_i|>=7w, and |z-n|>=7w. The standard contour
formula follows by residues at the nodes and n; its bound is independent
of how clustered the nodes are. At a node the error is exactly zero.
After summation against K_r and the phase, (5) contributes at most
2^((r+1)ell-1024Q)<2^(-p-20). This is a uniform absolute bound, including
arbitrary rational revivals and all cancellations.

## 3. Construct the interpolant with polynomial bits

Only ONE scalar needs numerical evaluation for the node values (its exact
rational expansion could have numerical K bits):

    b0=P_K(n_0),
    q_i=P_K(n_i)/P_K(n_0)
       =product_{t=0}^{i-1} (K-n_0-t)/(n_0+t+1).

Every q_i is an exactly computed positive rational of O(J ell) bits, with
q_i<=(K+1)^J. In the scaled variable x=(n-L)/M, write I_J(n)=b0 R_J(x),
where R_J interpolates these rational ratios. Its Lagrange basis is

    l_i(x)=product_{j!=i}(Mx-(n_j-L)) / [(-1)^(J-i) i!(J-i)!].

All node offsets lie in [0,M], so

    ||R_J||_1 <=(J+1)[2(K+1)^2]^J.                                  (6)

A common denominator is D_node J!, with
D_node=product_{t=0}^{J-1}(n_0+t+1). Each prefix denominator for q_i
divides D_node, and each i!(J-i)! divides J!. Thus this is a constructive
O(J(ell+log(J+1)))-bit denominator. Bound (6) also pays the numerator
bits. Dense exact polynomial construction is polynomial time; clustered
interpolation is not being treated as floating-point well conditioned.

Formula (1), with n=L+Mx, constructs the other polynomial exactly. Its
coefficient norm is at most (r+1)[4(K+1)]^r: each falling-factorial term
C(L+Mx,j) has coefficient norm <=(2K)^j/j!. A denominator r! suffices.
Therefore W(x)=R_J(x)K_r(K-L-Mx) has degree d=J+r and a constructive
common denominator D_node J! r!. All its coefficient bits are polynomial.
For the explicit integer

    E=bitlength(J+1)+J(1+2ell)+bitlength(r+1)+r(2+ell),

we have ||W||_1<=2^E. In particular, severe coefficient cancellation incurs
only E additional precision bits, not numerical K work.

## 4. Real Hiary calls, scalar precision and total clock

Write W(x)=sum_{j=0}^d w_j x^j. The retained approximating amplitude is

    b0/sqrt(C(K,r)) * e(A L+B L^2)
       * sum_{j=0}^d w_j F(M,j; A+2B L, B).                         (7)

This uses the ACTUAL normalized weights (k/M)^j in Hiary's real-argument
Theorem1.1. There is no missing M^j factor, no complex quadratic argument,
and no need to construct the large cyclotomic field of a/b. Rational phase
reduction, including the constant phase in (7), has polynomial bit cost.

Ask for absolute error 2^(-p-E-bitlength(d+1)-20) in each F. The checked
`2026-11-13-gaussian-chirp-review.md` supplies the source's polynomial error
prefactor conversion, exact rational branch choices, and deterministic
finite-bit clock. Equation (6) bounds the total weighted error. The exact
pre-scalar sum in (7) has modulus <=(K+1)2^E.

It suffices to compute b0, 1/sqrt(C(K,r)), and the unit phase to absolute
error 2^-P, where

    P=p+E+ell+bitlength(d+1)+50.

Clip the first two approximations to [0,1]. Square-root arithmetic uses the
already expanded O(r ell)-bit C(K,r). Compute b0 from

    log(b0)=log(K!)-log(n_0!)-log((K-n_0)!)-K log2.

The finite-bit logfactorial routine in `BINARY_FOCK_KERR_SAMPLING.md`
LF201–216 supplies polynomial(log K,P) evaluation: positive-real Stirling
with O(P+ell) terms and its first-omitted-term remainder, with a short
argument shift when necessary. Exact Bernoulli coefficients and the shift
products have polynomial bits. The extra ell guard bits pay multiplication
by K; no expanded K! or denominator 2^K is formed in this large-K branch.
If a scalar exponential is below the required absolute tolerance, it may
be clipped using a certified margin. No relative probability oracle is used.

Exact polynomial coefficients plus polynomially many guard bits pay the final
products/sum and final rounding. Combining scalar errors, Hiary errors, (5),
and the deleted tail leaves error <2^-p. Every degree, coefficient length,
requested precision, and call count is polynomial in Y,ell,p and phase bits.
All loops are explicitly bounded; there is no rejection or adaptive precision
search. This proves the statement, with the upper endpoint supplied by (2).

## Scope

The endpoint count Y may grow polynomially in log K and inverse sampling
accuracy; it is not a fixed constant. The result is stronger than the minimal
requested endpoint precision, since p is arbitrary and its cost is polynomial.
It does not prove the balanced bulk two-saddle construction, a balanced
sampler, a full CDF compiler, or anything for general passive angles. It does
not substitute a smooth distribution for the native count law. Those separate
operations retain their own normalization, coherence and precision obligations.

# Independent Gaussian-chirp / real-Hiary reduction review

13 November 2026. **Accepted at the absolute-error scope below**, with explicit
finite-bit details supplied here. Read current STATE/TRAPS, the full parent
`2026-11-13-gaussian-chirp-hiary-reduction.md`, and actual Hiary Theorem1.1
and section4 in `audits/sources/2026-11-13-one-pulse/hiary_theta.txt`.
No tests, implementation, network, API, Git, archive or shared-status edits.

## Exact statement

For binary integers L<=U and rationals alpha>=0, mu, a, b of total encoding
length B, and p>=1, the finite sum

    sum_{n=L}^U exp(-alpha(n-mu)^2) exp(2 pi i(an+bn^2))

has a deterministic absolute-2^-p approximation in polynomial(B,p) bit time,
using the constructive real-argument Hiary algorithm. There is no restriction
on numerical interval length, positive alpha, displacement mu, or proximity
of rational phase parameters to recursion boundaries. No relative-error or
normalized-distribution guarantee is included.

## Truncation and polynomial weight

Put H=U-L+1, h=bitlength(H), delta=2^-p, T=p+h+6. A nearest integer to mu,
clipped to [L,U], minimizes (n-mu)^2 there. Its exact rational test either
certifies an empty retained set or gives an interior starting point for two
monotone binary searches. Thus the condition alpha(n-mu)^2<=T finds its
entire retained interval with O(B) comparisons on polynomial-bit integers.
This includes mu far outside [L,U], arbitrarily tiny alpha, and huge alpha.
The discarded total modulus is at most H exp(-T)<=H 2^-T<delta/64.
Handle a singleton first; alpha=0 then uses Hiary after translation. A retained singleton is
one exponential with bounded real exponent and an exactly reduced phase.

For at least two retained integers set M=U0-L0>=1 and
Q(x)=alpha(L0+Mx-mu)^2. Both endpoints have Q<=T, hence convexity gives
0<=Q<=T on [0,1]. Write d=L0-mu. The endpoint inequalities imply
sqrt(alpha)|d|<=sqrt(T), sqrt(alpha)M<=2sqrt(T). Therefore

    alpha d^2<=T,  |2alpha dM|<=4T,  alpha M^2<=4T,

and ||Q||_1<=9T. This is valid even when mu is enormous and alpha tiny;
the potentially cancelling coefficients are computed exactly.

The parent's J=8(T+p+h+4) satisfies J+1>2eT. For
P_J(x)=sum_{l=0}^J (-Q(x))^l/l!, the REAL Lagrange remainder has derivative
factor exp(-xi)<=1. Thus

    sup |exp(-Q)-P_J| <= T^(J+1)/(J+1)! <=2^(-J-1)<delta/(64H).

Its contribution to the finite sum is <delta/64. Degree is at most 2J and
||P_J||_1<=exp(9T)<=2^(18T). These are coefficient-norm bounds, not an
assumption of numerically well-conditioned Taylor evaluation.

If Q has common denominator d_Q, then d_Q^J J! is a constructive common
denominator for every coefficient of P_J. Q's coefficient bit lengths are
O(B); consequently these denominators have O(J(B+log(J+1))) bits. The
coefficient-norm bound controls the numerators with an additional O(T) bits.
Exact dense polynomial arithmetic therefore has polynomial bit cost. It does
not generate exponentially long rational representations by repeated addition.

## Matching the actual source and finite precision

Writing P_J=sum c_j x^j and translating n=L0+k gives exactly

    exp(2 pi i(aL0+bL0^2))
      * sum_{j=0}^{2J} c_j F(M,j; a+2bL0, b),

where the actual source defines F as sum_{k=0}^M (k/M)^j times the quadratic
phase. There is NO missing M^j, 1/M, or interval-length normalization. At
j=0 the k=0 weight is1; Hiary explicitly adopts 0^0=1 (physical LF424).
All quadratic arguments remain real. The relevant primary locations are
LF62–95 (definition and Theorem1.1), LF1104–1198 (normalization and algorithm),
and LF1022–1045 (small-quadratic-argument boundary case).

Use the parent's zeta=2^(-p-18T-bitlength(2J+1)-8) as the allowed error per F.
Then sum |c_j| zeta<delta/256. The theorem's error is A1 nu^kappa1 eta,
not eta itself; the following allocation makes that conversion noncircular.
Fix source-dependent integers a0>=log2(max(1,A1)) and
s>=max(1,kappa1). Put

    q0=ceil(log2(1/zeta)), m=ceil(log2(M+1)),
    X=q0+m+j+a0+s+10,
    q=16(s+1)^2 X^2,  eta=2^-q.

Then nu=(j+1)log(M/eta)<=32 X^5, so log2(nu)<=3X (X>=10).
Hence A1 nu^kappa1 eta<=2^(a0+3sX-q)<=zeta/2. Every parameter and the
source's operation/operand-bit bounds remain polynomial(B,p). The constants
are fixed effective constants of its explicit analytic algorithm, not advice
depending on the input. This review does not claim optimized numerical values
for them or an implemented version of the source algorithm.

Exact-real input and floor decisions need no separation promise. One option
is to round both phase arguments, modulo1, to dyadics with
R=q0+3m+8 bits. Since (k/M)^j<=1,

    |partial_a F|<=pi M(M+1),
    |partial_b F|<=2 pi sum_{k=0}^M k^2.

The total perturbation is <=16(M+1)^3 2^-R<=zeta/16. This leaves room for
the preceding Hiary error. Rational phases could instead be retained exactly.

There is also a useful exact guard for Hiary's internal floor/ceiling branches.
Represent a normalized pair as a=A/D, b=C/D with common EVEN denominator D,
0<=A<D and 0<=C<=D/4. The nonboundary iteration b>0 sends the pair to

    a*=A/(2C),  b*=-D/(4C).

A common even denominator is D'=4C<=D, with numerators 2A and -D.
Integer reductions, conjugation, and the half-shifts of Lemma4.1 preserve that
denominator. Thus the denominators of these exact rational branch parameters
never grow; numerator reductions and floor(a+2bM) use polynomially many bits.
At b=0 the source uses its boundary procedure. In an iteration the new length
is floor(a+2bM)<1+M/2, so outside its explicit small-length cutoff there are
O(log(M+1)) iterations. This supplies an exact branch implementation even
arbitrarily close to an integer, rather than assuming rounded comparisons work.

The source's small-length case evaluates directly only when
M<=1000((j+1)log(M/eta))^6, which is polynomial in the charged parameters.
It does not silently enumerate a binary-large interval. Elementary exponential
and logarithm evaluation at its stated polynomial operand precision has
polynomial bit cost; source section4 supplies the finite algorithm and clock.

## Assembly and boundary of the result

Keep the rational c_j exact, or round them with their explicitly bounded
product magnitudes included. Each F has modulus<=M+1; intermediate products
and sums need O(18T+h) integer bits and polynomially many fractional guard bits.
The exact coefficient denominator storage above is separately charged.
Reduce aL0+bL0^2 modulo1 exactly, and approximate its unit complex phase to
delta/[16(H+1)]. The true polynomial-weight sum has modulus at most H+delta/64,
so this phase error contributes <delta/8. Polynomially allocated rounding,
the two truncation errors, and the F errors leave total error strictly <delta.

The parent statement survives; no counterexample or change of hypotheses is
needed. This closes Gaussian damping of a finite quadratic chirp ONLY. It
does not pay binomial/Krawtchouk approximation, confluent derivatives, bilinear
Cauchy sums, a native count CDF, rejection probabilities, or photon sampling.

# Binary-Fock Kerr circuits: prior-art endpoint and classical branch attack

7 November2026. CLOSED written quantum/classical composition with three
independent reviews read by the parent. Quantum endpoint is known prior art.
The bounded-branch bunched-input classical sampler is a written theorem,
not an implemented or executed sampler; exact finite controls are separate.

## Question, selection and native model

The question is whether binary-large occupation and a few non-Gaussian Kerr
phases give a sampling advantage after all access, cutoff and classical
baselines are charged. This is an end-to-end count-sampling problem, not a
new optical backend or a quantum-state preparation oracle.

Take0<epsilon<=1/4 without loss of generality. Input: m modes, binary nonnegative occupations n_i with total K, an explicit
list of L gates, and requested TV error epsilon. A gate is a two-mode passive
beam splitter B(theta)=exp(theta(a†b-b†a)), a number phase, or local Kerr
K_{a/b}=exp(2pi i (a/b) binom(n,2)), with rational angles in turns, binary
numerators/positive denominators. The desired output is one photon-count
vector distributed within epsilon of the ideal circuit. All input/angle
bits, list length, m and output m log(K+1) bits are charged. A stronger
unitary statement concerns arbitrary reference-entangled input of total K.
No squeezed/displaced input, loss, preparation oracle or binary-compressed
repeat count is included. L is the ACTUAL listed gate count.

The mechanism is common-grid quantum Hermite transforms around passive
optical operations, plus reversible modular arithmetic for Kerr phases.
Expected quantum target: poly(native bits, log(K+1), log(L/epsilon)) gates.
That target is already claimed by Prakash etal2610.03581v1 Corollary2.3:
this is PRIOR ART, not a new algorithm. The narrower number-conserving proof
below makes its native cutoff and coherent phase contract concrete.
No novelty, quantum/classical separation, practicality or execution claimed.

Before selection, corpus been-tried/baselines and actual primary literature
were checked for binary-spin/Krawtchouk, binary-Fock Kerr and bunched revival
sampling. The baseline catalog's irrelevant SDP hit is not a scientific
comparator. Current sparse-constant relations, growing-rank surface readout
and Gaudin-gap routes were independently compared: no paid constant map,
succinct cover readout or quantitative physical gap operation emerged.
A fixed-spectrum Cauchy Lax matrix admits spurious non-Bethe vectors and
therefore does not supply the Gaudin gap; no physical gap counterexample.

Strong classical comparators: explicit Fock evolution/permanent sampling,
small tensor width, Gaussian-positive-Wigner methods only on their genuine
state/measurement domain, bunched passive multinomial sampling, terminal
number-diagonal phases, and the coherent finite-branch sampler proved below.
A large bosonic Hilbert space is not evidence of hardness. Kerr Fourier
branches are coherent and cannot simply be classically mixed.

## 1. Paid known quantum endpoint

Actual sources retained under audits/sources/binary_fock_kerr/:
Iyer2602.15180v1 Lemma3.1, Theorem4.2 and its phase/label-erasure proof;
Prakash2610.03581v1 Theorems2.1/2.2 and Corollary2.3. Their PDFs, text and
SHA256 manifests are separate. This is a source-based written construction,
not independent execution of QHT or an independently implemented circuit.

Use one two-mode product QHT and operational grid for all local pair totals
at most K. Iyer Lemma3.1 uses the same discrete quadratic-chirp unitary on
each Fock input, with exponentially small grid error. Its proof accounts
for the high-energy intermediate SHEARS: only the complete beam splitter
conserves number, so a naive K truncation of every shear is invalid.
Theorem4.2 explicitly maps arbitrary superpositions and fixes Hermite phase
+1, then erases the occupation workspace coherently. Thus there is no
measurement or arbitrary fixed-spin-dependent phase. Source sign convention
requires exp(-2i theta A_12); Prakash BSY has the opposite sign.

There are d=(K+1)(K+2)/2 triangular two-mode input basis states. A common
per-column grid error delta gives restricted operator error<=sqrt(d)delta,
so delta=O(eta/(K+1)) pays all superpositions and references. Uniform QHT
operator errors telescope separately. The required grid size is polynomial
in K and1/eta, so its qubit count and the source gate cost remain polynomial
in log(K+1),log(1/eta). Choose one sufficiently padded cutoff/grid per gate.
If using the WHOLE rectangle n_a,n_b<=K, the inverse needs cutoff2K+1;
the native fixed-global-K proof only needs the triangle and cutoffK+1.

The original Hermite2510.04929 Theorem19 and Lemmas25--27 explicitly cover
coherent superpositions, a common amplification polynomial and degree-label
erasure. Pad its effective cutoff N_eff>=max(K+1,C log1/eta) to respect
N>log1/eta. Where the source bounds a squared tail bytau, use internal
tau=O(eta²). Both choices keep grid size polynomial and gate cost logarithmic
inK and1/eta. Its temporarily dropped(-1)^n Hermite convention must be
restored if needed; product parity commutes with a number-conserving mixer.

Reduce beam-splitter angles modulo2pi, never modulo pi while dropping
B(theta+pi)=(-1)^(n_a+n_b)B(theta). Local pair totals can be coherently
superposed even at fixed GLOBAL totalK. Number phases and Kerr phases are
computed by binary arithmetic; compute a*binom(n,2) mod b exactly, synthesize
the rational phase to eta and uncompute work. Exact modular arithmetic does
not mean arbitrary-angle synthesis is exact. All angle BIT lengths count.

Per-stage clean-isometry error O(epsilon/L) yields full errorO(epsilon) by
hybrid telescoping along the ideal total-K trajectory. Earlier digital
leakage is included in this operator error; no postselection or conditional
renormalization. Number measurement contracts trace distance. Map an invalid
padding tuple deterministically to the original valid input tuple; since
the ideal output is valid, this does not increase TV error. Initial binary
Fock preparation/output costO(m log(K+1)). K0 is trivial vacuum.

## 2. Exact interference and universality scope controls

Let K_pi(n)=exp(pi i binom(n,2)). It is1 on n0,1 and-1 on n2. For a balanced
B, the operation C=B†(K_pi tensor K_pi)B acts on the pair input states
00,10,01,11 as diag(1,1,1,-1), with zero leakage. In the two-photon sector
B|11> is a NOON state supported on20,02; both terms acquire-1. Total0/1
are unchanged. Apply this gadget between selected rails of two dual-rail
qubits. Native passive single-qubit rotations/phases plus this exact CZ
contain the usual universal gate set. Thus a general efficient classical
constant-TV sampler would simulate BQP sampling (and BQP decision with a
fixed sufficient error margin). This is a known-universality implication,
not proof BPP!=BQP, sampling hardness, novelty or an exponential separation.
It already uses small occupations and does not arise from high K alone.

For K_pi, period4 Fourier coefficients are
    c=(0,(1-i)/2,0,(1+i)/2),
    K_pi(n)=sum_r c_r exp(2pi i r n/4).
An exact two-photon witness is
    |20> -> B(pi/4) -> K_pi on modea -> B(pi/8)†.
Its output is -|11>, hence counts(0,1,0) in basis(02,11,20). The incoherent
Fourier mixture instead has probabilities(1/4,1/2,1/4), TVdistance1/2.
A spectator-mode control keeps globaltotal1 while pairtotals0,1 are
superposed; reducing B(pi) toidentity makes the two final states orthogonal.

These identities are frozen in audits/controls/binary_fock_kerr/control.py
and result.json using exact Sage algebraic arithmetic. They do not execute
QHT, prove the large-K gate bound or establish complexity separation.

## 3. Constructive classical branch sampler

Restrict only this CLASSICAL theorem to a bunched input |K,0,...,0> (the
occupied mode can be specified). Keep arbitrary passive gates and rational
Kerr gates. For Kerr j choose q_j=2b_j after fraction reduction; an identity
phase may useq_j1. The exact period dividesq_j. Fourier expansion gives

    K_j(n)=sum_(r<q_j) c_jr exp(2pi i r n/q_j),
    c_jr=q_j^-1 sum_(u<q_j) K_j(u) exp(-2pi i r u/q_j),
    sum_r |c_jr|²=1.

After expanding t Kerr gates there are chi=product_j q_j indexed branches.
Each branch is an ordinary passive interferometer U_r with coefficientc_r,
where sum_r |c_r|²=1 even if some branches coincide. The actual state is
Phi=sum_r c_r psi_r and has norm1 because the original circuit is unitary.
Here psi_r is a normalized bosonic condensate with one-particle vector
alpha_r=U_r e_input. Its count amplitude is exactly

    psi_r(x)=sqrt(K!/product_i x_i!) product_i alpha_ri^(x_i), sum_i x_i=K.

Its probabilities are multinomial, efficiently sampled by m-1 BINOMIAL
samples with binary totals. Its complex amplitude, including signs/phases,
can be evaluated to polynomial requested BIT precision with logfactorials
and binary angle multiplication; it is not a permanent of sizeK.

Choose a branch uniformly from the chi indices, then sample x from its
multinomial law. The proposal is p(x)=S(x)/chi, S=sum_r |psi_r(x)|². Accept
with probability
    A(x)=|sum_r c_r psi_r(x)|²/S(x).
Cauchy-Schwarz and sum|c|²1 imply0<=A<=1. The accepted distribution is
EXACTLY the desired count law, with acceptanceprobability1/chi. This
retains interference; it is not the incorrect Fourier mixture in section2.
Finite numerical normalization is paid below. Runtime polynomial in chi,
m,L, nativebitlength,log(K+1),log(1/epsilon); hence polynomial in nativebits
when chi is polynomial. An exponentially large chi is charged, not ignored.
Constantly many low-denominator Kerr phases are a natural covered case.
The universality gadget has chi exponential in the number of nonlinear gates,
so this classical theorem does not dequantize all native circuits.
